verdict.summary: OAuth apps are self-serve from a separate Calendly developer account, with sandbox and production app types and no Calendly review found in the docs. The catches are plan-based: any Calendly user can authorize and read data, but webhooks and the Scheduling API need the end user to be on a paid plan, Free users get 50 requests/min, and refresh tokens became single-use (enforced from 31 Aug 2026).

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Sign up for a developer account with GitHub or Google, create a Sandbox app with an http://localhost redirect, run PKCE.

timeToProd.assumes: A Production OAuth app reading scheduled events and invitees (and webhooks for paid-plan users); no listing in Calendly's integrations directory.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Neither the app-creation nor scopes pages mention a Calendly review or approval step; 'no review' is our reading of their absence.

verdict.cost: Free to create apps. Webhooks and the Scheduling API need the connecting user to be on a paid Calendly plan; some compliance endpoints are Enterprise-only.

prerequisites.item: A Calendly developer account (separate from a Calendly user account), signed up with GitHub or Google
prerequisites.why: OAuth apps are created and managed there.

prerequisites.item: An HTTPS redirect URI for the Production app
prerequisites.why: Production redirect URIs must be HTTPS; Sandbox allows http://localhost.

prerequisites.item: A Calendly user account on a paid plan for testing webhooks
prerequisites.why: Webhooks and the Scheduling API need Professional, Standard, Teams, Enterprise or similar paid plans.

scopeTiers.tier: Read scheduling data (works on all plans)
scopeTiers.impact: Enough for an agent to read a user's meetings and availability. New apps get no API access until scopes are requested and the user approves them; users can decline scopes at install.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: That the user (not Calendly) does the approving is our reading; the page doesn't say who approves.

scopeTiers.impact: Personal data of people who booked; the scopes page suggests invitees:read alongside scheduled_events:read for syncing.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: invitees:read appears in a search snippet of the scopes page but not in the catalog list we fetched; confirm the exact scope name.

scopeTiers.impact: Webhooks and the Scheduling API only work for users on paid plans, so Free users fall back to polling within 50 requests/min.
Activity logs and data deletion endpoints are Enterprise-only; organization-level scopes need an org admin to authorize.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: The org-admin requirement is our inference.

steps.title: Create a Calendly developer account
steps.detail: Sign up on the developer portal with GitHub or Google.

steps.title: Create a Sandbox OAuth app
steps.detail: Choose web or native, Sandbox environment, redirect URI (http://localhost is OK in Sandbox), and scopes. Copy the client secret and webhook signing key immediately; they aren't shown again.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: developer.calendly.com/console/apps returned HTTP 200 on 2026-10-20; we did not sign in.

steps.title: Implement auth code + PKCE (S256)
steps.detail: Send users to https://auth.calendly.com/oauth/authorize (redirects to calendly.com/oauth/authorize) with code_challenge and S256, then POST to https://auth.calendly.com/oauth/token. PKCE is recommended for web apps and expected for native apps.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: Authorize URL returned 301 to calendly.com/oauth/authorize; token endpoint with no body returned invalid_request 'Missing required parameter: grant_type.'

steps.title: Handle single-use refresh tokens
steps.detail: Access tokens last 2 hours. Each successful refresh revokes the old refresh token and returns a new one; persist it atomically and serialize refreshes per user. Reuse returns invalid_grant.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The 2-hour lifetime comes from a search snippet of Calendly's authentication how-to page, which returned 404 when we fetched it.

steps.title: Build data sync with webhooks or polling
steps.detail: For paid-plan users, subscribe to webhooks and verify signatures with the signing key. For Free users, poll scheduled events within 50 requests/user/min.

steps.title: Test with Free and paid user accounts
steps.detail: Authorize from a Free user and a paid user to confirm the plan-gated paths (webhooks, Scheduling API) degrade cleanly.

steps.title: Create the Production app
steps.detail: Create a second app with environment Production, an HTTPS redirect URI, and the same least-privilege scopes. Store the new client secret and signing key.

steps.title: Ship and monitor token health
steps.detail: Alert on invalid_grant spikes (lost refresh races) and 429s; respect the 8 token requests per user per minute limit.

agentCanDo: Implement PKCE auth and single-use refresh token handling
Pick least-privilege scopes from the catalog
Build webhook ingestion with signature checks and a polling fallback for Free users
humanMustDo: Sign up for the developer account with GitHub or Google

blockers.cause: Refresh tokens are single-use; a refresh token was reused, often by two concurrent workers.
blockers.fix: Lock refresh per user, store the new refresh token atomically, and re-prompt if it still fails.

blockers.symptom: API calls return no data or a permission error on a newly created app
blockers.cause: New apps get no API access until scopes are requested and approved; the user may have declined some scopes.
blockers.fix: Request needed scopes explicitly and handle partial grants.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Exact error string not documented on the page we read.

blockers.symptom: Webhook subscription fails for some users
blockers.cause: Webhooks need a paid Calendly plan.
blockers.fix: Detect the plan and fall back to polling scheduled events.

blockers.cause: Per-user limits: 500/min on paid plans, 50/min on Free, and stricter caps on Create Event Invitee.
blockers.fix: Wait for the reset (typically 60 seconds) and use exponential backoff.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The 60-second reset comes from a search snippet.

blockers.symptom: Production app rejects your localhost redirect
blockers.cause: Production redirect URIs must be HTTPS.
blockers.fix: Keep localhost on the Sandbox app and use HTTPS for Production.

nuances.text: Single-use refresh tokens are enforced from 31 Aug 2026 for new apps, with a grace period for older apps that Calendly says will end.
Legacy OAuth apps and personal access tokens from before scoped permissions keep full access, and legacy tokens migrate to scoped tokens on refresh without reauthorization.
Rate limits apply per user and count third-party integrations too, so other tools the user connects share their quota.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: 'Counts third-party integrations' comes from a search snippet of the rate limits page.

nuances.text: Create Event Invitee (booking on someone's behalf) is capped at 10/min, 50/hour and 100/day per user on paid non-Enterprise plans, and 5/day on trials, which limits AI booking agents.
The client secret and webhook signing key are shown once at creation.
